messages:
maya: quick share — ran a small bring-up for ozma-lite-13b @ q4f16 + a new speculative scheduler (fastspec-v2). wanted to dump numbers and get quick reactions.

conor: nice, what was the workload?

maya: ran 5k samples from `prod-sim-qa` (questions + multi-turn context avg 120 tokens). compared: baseline (no-spec, q4f16), fastspec-v1, fastspec-v2. each run on the same Dedicated pool (A100s, same batch shapes).

li: TL;DR?

maya: TL;DR: latency down ~28% median, p95 down ~18% vs baseline. token-efficiency improved. but automatic quality metrics show a small regress on BLEURT and answer-coverage on long-contexts. human spot-check flagged 6/100 hallucinations (baseline 2/100).

ana: can you paste the numbers?

maya: sure — here's the perf/quality extract:

```
Model            | median_latency | p95_latency | tokens_per_req | BLEURT_delta | halluc_rate
-----------------|----------------|-------------|----------------|--------------|------------
baseline q4f16   | 220ms          | 480ms       | 1.00           | 0.0          | 2%         
fastspec-v1 q4f16| 175ms (-20%)   | 420ms (-12%)| 0.94           | -0.7         | 4%         
fastspec-v2 q4f16| 158ms (-28%)   | 399ms (-17%)| 0.88           | -1.6         | 6%         
```

Notes: BLEURT_delta is relative to baseline (higher is better). halluc_rate measured by a simple heuristic + rapid human spot-check.

mitra: thanks — sounds promising but quality delta is non-trivial. how deterministic is the halluc measurement? 6/100 is small sample.

maya: agreed. the automated halluc detector is conservative (precision ~0.85) on this dataset. human spot-check was 6/100 flagged from the detector, then manually confirmed 5/6 as genuine hallucinations.

conor: what about prompt-sensitivity? maybe fastspec-v2 is more brittle on long-turn attention windows.

maya: good call. I sliced by context-length: the regressions concentrate on >200 token contexts. for <100 tokens, BLEURT delta is -0.3 and halluc_rate comparable to baseline. for >200 tokens BLEURT delta -2.2 and halluc_rate 10%.

li: any logs/example of failure?

maya: pasted a short anonymized sample below (redacted):

```
User: "Summarize the meeting notes and list action items with owners."
Baseline: lists 5 specifc action items with owners and timestamps.
fastspec-v2: merges two distinct action items, invents "send compliance report" (not in transcript).
```

mitra: that aligns with prefix-misselection / premature early-exit behavior. fastspec may be aborting generation and relying on learned priors.

conor: did you try hybrid fallback (fastspec for short contexts, baseline for long)?

maya: yes — quick routing rule: context_len > 180 -> baseline; else fastspec-v2. That recovers most of the quality and keeps ~15% median latency win across the traffic mix (weighed by production context histogram).

ana: how about token-matching coverage for RAG cases (where exact quoting matters)?

maya: RAG snippets are sensitive. fastspec-v2 shows 1.8% exact-match drop on retrieval-quote tasks. not acceptable for strict quoting customers.

li: ops-bot any capacity / infra concerns for rolling this as experiment?

ops-bot: deploy-check: Dedicated pool has headroom for a canary at 5% traffic. Autoscale alarms unchanged. No config drift detected for the test cluster.

conor: suggested next steps: 1) expand eval set to 20k with stratified long-context samples, 2) run human eval focused on halluc/precision, 3) tweak commitment thresholds in fastspec-v2 (make it more conservative), 4) test hybrid routing policy in canary.

maya: plan I'll run: (a) run 20k stratified eval overnight, (b) try two conservative thresholds (+0.1, +0.25 logit margin) and report, (c) prep canary routing rule.

mitra: add a focused RAG holdout and a few strict-exact-match testcases — we should gate by that for customers with quoting needs.

li: anything else for eval methodology? I'd suggest logging per-token speculative-abort positions and KV cache hit patterns so we can debug early-exit causes.

maya: adding that to the eval plan. also will export a random seed sample for reproducibility.

conor: thanks — if overnight run looks ok, we can set a 5% canary with hybrid routing and a rollback guard tied to BLEURT -1.0 or halluc_rate > 4% absolute.

maya: noted. I'll post results tomorrow morning. thanks for the rapid feedback :thumbsup:

mitra: ping me if you need help crafting the human eval rubric.

maya: will do.

ops-bot: scheduled run job `spec-fast_eval_9501234567` queued, expected completion in ~9h.
